header.title: pBrooklyn 47.218.156 ("Le Papyrus Magique Illustré"): AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Temple library papyri
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:egy:tla:bbawtempelbib:pbrooklyn-47-218-156-le-papyrus-magique-illustre:translit, from the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (2018), in Simon Schweitzer's AED-TEI (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. notes.1.10: ḏdft, 'creeping things', taken as reptiles. dn in 'great, dn form' is not understood. swjw is an unidentified animal. dbjw taken as hippopotamus (db). rḫt is the lapwing (rekhyt), also 'the common people'. sfd ds, 'knives that slaughter', is partly uncertain.
notes.1.38: mnty is not understood. The šꜣjw, Khadjaruti, Shaaruti and the ꜥmꜣt of the West are demonesses with foreign-sounding names; ꜥmꜣt may be 'swallower', or, as written ꜥꜣmt later in this papyrus, 'Asiatic woman'. ꜥ, literally 'arm', is a demonic seizure; jw/jwt taken as 'evildoer'. ḥmwt-rʾ, 'craft of the mouth', is sorcery.
notes.2.11: swjw is an unidentified animal. Heh (Ḥḥ) is the god of millions; 'a Heh of horns' may mean 'millions of horns'. tnḥw taken as 'wings' (dnḥ); pš and qn in 2.17-2.18 are not understood. rwbꜣšꜣ is a foreign word, perhaps 'garment, armour' (compare Semitic lbš). ꜥꜣmt is written ꜥmꜣt elsewhere in this papyrus. stj, 'shoot, pour', is also used of semen. thnt (t restored) and the '30' are not understood. bꜣrw (dual) is unidentified; msd nk, 'hates copulation', is uncertain.
notes.2.32: ḏꜣm n mꜣꜥt, 'papyrus of truth', perhaps genuine or fine papyrus.

nodes.text: If any living reptile sees him, they die at once.

They cannot live in the [presence] of your great, *dn* form, which has nine faces on a single neck: one with the face of Bes, one with the face of a *swjw*, one with the face of a falcon, one with the face of a crocodile, one with the face of a hippopotamus, one with the face of a lion, one with the face of a bull, one with the face of a baboon, one with the face of a cat.
[Behold], [your] [body] is [as] a *rekhyt*-bird, with 4 wings [and] [4] arms;
your back is a falcon, the toes [of] your feet are uraei, your arms bear eyes, slaughtering knives are in your hands, life, stability and dominion are in your strong arm.
You will not let [any] evil impurity have power over him; you will drive back [all] the evil magic they have made against him, he being pure [...] in your [great(?)] name.
Words to be spoken over this image [which is] [in] [drawing], [drawn] [on] new [papy]rus, [placed] [at] [the throat] [of] a woman or a child.
[It is what] [rescues] [them] [from] [...] against [every(?)] *mnty* [...] [driving] away dead man, dead woman, sorcery.
The drawings of the Bes of seven faces.
It is made to drive away a dead man, a dead woman, a male enemy, a female enemy, a male adversary, a female adversary, the *šꜣjw*, the *ꜥmꜣ[t]* of the West; to drive away a dead woman.

Words to be spoken: Stop, you, male adversary, female adversary, Khadjaruti, Shaaruti, *ꜥmꜣt* of the West, every fear, every *ꜥ*-stroke of a male or female evildoer(?), dead man, dead woman, male adversary, female adversary, male enemy, female enemy, who would come against Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, by night, by day, at any time of every day.

But if you let them raise their arms [against] [Pharaoh], may he live, prosper and be healthy, they will [raise] their [arms] against the man of a million [cubits], who has 7 faces on a single [neck]: one with the face of Bes, one with the face of a *swjw*, one with the face of a falcon, one with the face of a snake, one with the face of a lion, one with the face of a jackal,
with Heh upon his head,
his back a falcon,
his tail that of a crocodile,
his phallus standing up, strong,
his arms bearing 8 wings(?),
with 4 *pš*,
with 4 *qn* on him(?),
he being equipped with a *rubasha*,
with a Heh of horns set upon his head.
If the eye of any living person sees him, they die, they catch fire, and their hearts burn.

Ho! Ho! Amun-Ra, lord of the thrones of the Two Lands, come, stand against the male and female adversary, Khidjaruti, Shaaruti, the *ꜥꜣmt* of the West, every fear, every *ꜥ*-stroke of a male or female evildoer(?), dead man, dead woman, male and female enemy, and every evil and bad thing that would come against Pharaoh, may he live, prosper and be healthy, [to] copulate with him, to shoot into him in his ears, to do every evil and bad thing against him.
If they raise their arms against him, they raise their arms against the man of a million cubits, who stands upon the *[t]hnt* of 30 of the land of Kush,
his two *barw* being deep red, [he] hating copulation(?).
Words to be spoken over this image, which is drawn in drawing on true papyrus, placed at the throat of a man.
It is what rescues him from dead man, dead woman, male and female adversary, sorcery, the Khidjaruti, Shaaruti, the *ꜥꜣmt* of the West, from every evil and bad thing.
